# EyeDataHub

> Versioned command-line access tool backed by a manually curated snapshot of
> 386 ophthalmology data resources across 18 categories.

EyeDataHub helps software clients find, inspect, cite, preflight, and acquire
supported resources from official hosts. It does not host third-party data,
accept agreements for a user, or determine legal permission, ethics, data
quality, or scientific suitability. Access friction, acquisition automation,
and source-stated terms are separate fields; unknown values remain unknown.

## Read first

- [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md): canonical repository guide.
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): cross-tool pointer.
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md): reviewed contribution requirements.
- [DATASETS.md](DATASETS.md): current counts and operational boundaries.
- [llms-full.txt](llms-full.txt): compact record-level catalog.
- [catalog guide](DATASETS.md): catalog fields, access terms, and command examples.

## Structured interfaces

- `eyehub search --json`: deterministic, read-only catalog search.
- `eyehub show <name> --json`: full record and dated verification fields.
- `eyehub cite <name> --type {dataset,article,software} --format json`:
  object-specific citations and identifiers.
- `eyehub preflight <name> --json`: source terms, evidence, access
  requirements, route, intended behavior, and warnings; no transfer.
- `eyehub download <name> --data-dir <path> --dry-run --json`: explicit
  acquisition plan; no transfer in dry-run mode.
- `eyehub download <name> --data-dir <path>`: supported official-source
  transfer and local provenance manifest.
- `from eyedatahub.datasets.registry import REGISTRY`: direct Python access;
  `REGISTRY` is a retained internal compatibility name.
- `python -m eyedatahub.agent.mcp_server`: optional read-only MCP access to the
  shared metadata implementation.

Use `eyedatahub` for Python imports and `eyehub` for CLI commands.

## Guardrails

- Search, show, cite, Python, JSON, and MCP operations are read-only.
- Transfer starts only through an explicit non-dry-run download command.
- Never bypass authentication, click-through, manual approval, author-contact,
  institutional, or geographic controls.
- Never infer dataset-file terms from a paper, website, mirror, or code
  license. Inspect the recorded scope and official evidence.
- A source-term group is descriptive and does not establish permission.
- A loader label is not evidence of a complete live download; inspect
  `acquisition_support`, `loader_test_scope`, and `loader_test_result`.
- Never put credentials or third-party dataset files in issues, pull requests,
  logs, manifests, or the EyeDataHub repository.
